title: Will GSP Comeback and Fight Khabib?
guestName: Will GSP Comeback and Fight Khabib?
guestBio: Taken from MMA Show #107 w/Georges St-Pierre:
tldr: Georges St-Pierre gives his honest analysis of how a potential matchup with Khabib Nurmagomedov would have played out stylistically
GSP discusses the specific challenges Khabib's mat pressure would have created for even an elite wrestler of his caliber
Conversation about the striking game, with GSP arguing his offensive output on the feet would have been a meaningful factor
Behind-the-scenes discussion of how close the fight actually came to being made and why the weight class conversation never resolved
Joe and GSP explore which version of each fighter, at what weight, would have produced the most competitive matchup
Reflections on why the GSP vs. Khabib hypothetical remains one of MMA's most discussed and genuinely unresolvable debates
recap:
Georges St-Pierre, arguably the greatest welterweight of all time and one of the most technically complete fighters in MMA history, joins Joe Rogan on the MMA Show to discuss a matchup that fans have dreamed about for years: GSP coming back to fight Khabib Nurmagomedov.

St-Pierre approaches the conversation with the careful, analytical mindset that defined his entire career. He isn't interested in selling a fantasy version of the fight. He walks through the real challenges. Khabib is an elite wrestler with phenomenal pressure and top control who had never been seriously hurt and never been stopped. GSP, while one of the best wrestlers ever in MMA, would be stepping up in weight against a man engineered specifically to dominate on the ground.

The conversation gets interesting when GSP discusses his advantages. His striking game at the highest level was elite, and Khabib's willingness to trade on the feet was sometimes a liability. If GSP could keep the fight standing or neutralize the takedowns long enough to work his own offensive game, the matchup looks considerably different. GSP's size when competing at middleweight and his ability to dictate pace were factors he believes would have been relevant at 155 as well.

Joe pushes on the Khabib wrestling. GSP is honest: Khabib's mat pressure is unlike anything he faced in the welterweight division. The ground-and-pound from top position alone would have required GSP to implement a defensive game plan he'd have to build specifically for that matchup.

They talk about whether the fight was ever truly close to happening. There were discussions at various points during GSP's 2017 comeback run, but weight class logistics and contract realities never aligned properly. GSP says the conversation wasn't as serious as media coverage made it appear at the time.

The clip closes with Joe and GSP agreeing that the fight is one of MMA's great hypotheticals: a matchup that's genuinely interesting precisely because both fighters were so dominant in their eras that there's no comfortable answer for who wins.
